title: Chicken drumstick, baked or broiled, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken drumstick prepared by baking or broiling in a fast‑food/restaurant setting. The meat is tender and relatively low in fat when the skin is omitted. Often served as a single portion in combo meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks contain more iron than breast meat because of the darker muscle.
Baking without skin reduces calories by roughly 30 % compared with skin‑on versions.
Fast‑food chains frequently marinate drumsticks beforehand to speed up cooking.
Drumsticks are commonly paired with dipping sauces, enhancing their appeal.
Internal temperature should reach 165 °F (74 °C) for safe consumption.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Skinless drumstick provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Removing the skin cuts saturated fat content, which is beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, which support bone health and immunity.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The high protein level helps you feel full longer after a meal.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor salmonella; ensure proper cooking temperature.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people can be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Restaurant preparations often add salt and sauces, increasing sodium intake.

items.title: High glycemic impact of sauces
items.content: Sweet dipping sauces can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the drumstick by pulling the meat off the bone with your hands. Serve with vegetable sides, fries, or a salad. Sauces are optional, but watch the amount of added salt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool cooked drumsticks to 4 °C within 2 hours and keep refrigerated for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months; thaw in the refrigerator before reheating.
